title: 1 eVTOL Stock to Buy, and 1 to Avoid
author: Jeff Siegel
description: Joby Aviation is recommended as the stronger eVTOL investment due to its advanced FAA certification progress, 50,000+ test flight miles, strategic partnerships with Delta and Virgin Atlantic, and strong cash position of $1.1 billion. Archer Aviation is advised to be avoided despite high-profile partnerships, as much of its valuation assumes successful execution and it faces significant risks in certification, manufacturing scaling, and commercialization.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Leading certification progress with 50,000+ test flight miles, FAA-conforming production aircraft, established partnerships with Delta Air Lines and Virgin Atlantic, international expansion in Japan and UAE, strong balance sheet with $1.1 billion in cash, and direct control over operations positioning it as the strongest competitor in the eVTOL market.

title: Prediction: Delta Air Lines Stock Will Prove Wall Street Right and Hit $100 by 2028
author: Lee Samaha
description: Delta Air Lines is positioned to reach $100 per share by 2028, supported by Wall Street's $108 consensus target. The airline has demonstrated resilience by diversifying revenue streams through premium cabins, ancillary services, and loyalty programs, allowing it to absorb significant fuel cost increases while maintaining strong free cash flow guidance of $3-4 billion for 2026. With a forward P/E ratio of 11.5-13.2x and management's stress test showing profitability even with $4 billion in additional fuel costs, Delta appears less cyclical than typical airline stocks.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The article presents a bullish case for Delta, highlighting its ability to diversify income streams, absorb fuel cost pressures, maintain strong free cash flow guidance, and trade at attractive valuations (11.5-13.2x forward P/E). The company is characterized as less cyclical than peers and positioned to reach $100 per share, aligning with Wall Street consensus.
United is mentioned briefly as a peer that has similarly made efforts to diversify income streams, but no specific analysis or sentiment is provided about the company itself.

title: This Beaten-Down Aviation Stock Is Worth a Look Despite Its 46% Decline
author: Steven Porrello
description: Joby Aviation's stock has declined 47% year-to-date, but the article argues this presents a buying opportunity for long-term investors. Despite slow regulatory progress, Joby has made significant operational advances including thousands of test miles, strategic partnerships with Toyota, Delta, and Uber, and participation in a White House-backed eVTOL program. The author views the stock as a speculative long-term play with potential for substantial gains if the urban air mobility market reaches projected valuations.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Despite significant stock decline, the article highlights improving business prospects including regulatory progress, strategic partnerships, operational achievements, and long-term market potential. The author recommends it as a compelling long-term speculative buy for aggressive investors.

title: Here's Why FTAI Aviation Stock Was Red Hot in the First Half of 2026
author: Lee Samaha
description: FTAI Aviation stock surged 37.4% in H1 2026 despite volatility driven by AI investment, Iran conflict, and energy prices. The company operates three businesses: engine maintenance, aviation leasing, and the nascent FTAI Power division converting legacy aircraft engines into data center power turbines. While a CFM56 parts agreement with CFM International is positive, rising jet fuel prices from geopolitical tensions have reduced flight departure forecasts, creating near-term headwinds. FTAI Power revenue is expected to begin in 2027.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong H1 2026 performance (+37.4%), strategic CFM56 parts agreement with CFM International, and promising FTAI Power business launching in 2027 with data center exposure. Long-term growth prospects are excellent despite near-term headwinds from elevated jet fuel prices.

title: DAX, FTSE 100 Forecast: 2 Trades to Watch
author: Fiona Cincotta
description: The DAX has reached record highs, benefiting from a rotation out of US tech into European cyclicals and industrials, which offer better valuations. The FTSE 100 has broken above its symmetrical triangle pattern with M&A activity in focus, including EasyJet's takeover by Castlelake and ITV's sale of its media business to Sky. Both indices are well-positioned as investors question the sustainability of the AI-driven rally and seek value in European equities.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Agreed to sell media and entertainment business to Sky for £1.6 billion, creating a larger UK-focused streaming platform better positioned to compete with global rivals like Netflix and Prime Video.

Accepted takeover offer from Castlelake after months of speculation, ending uncertainty. The acquisition follows weakness in share price due to higher fuel costs and softer travel demand, providing a positive resolution for shareholders.
